name: SLOSH
description: Slosh is a four-handed British domino game from the Trains family, played with a double-six set. The engine tile is placed in the center; each player has a train (a line of tiles) extending from the engine toward them. On your turn you add a tile to your own train if you can; if you cannot, the next player may slosh (play on your train) then play on their own. The round ends when someone dominoes or the game is blocked; lowest pip count in hand wins the round. Scoring is with poker chips or pencil.

British member of the Trains family. The name refers to water or liquid spilling over (sloshing), evoking splashing someone at a bar.
Four players. A four-handed British domino game; each player has their own train extending from the center engine toward them, and play proceeds to the left.
Double-six domino set. Each player receives six tiles; four tiles form the boneyard and are not used in the round.
Double-six domino set, markers or poker chips (or pencil) for scoring.

Each player gets six tiles. The engine for the first round is the double-four; if it is in the boneyard, the hand is redealt until someone has it. The player with the engine places it first; play proceeds to the left.
